attempts.label: DANDI:001131
attempts.paper_title: A line attractor encoding a persistent internal state requires neuropeptide signaling
attempts.entry_title: VMHvl Esr1 activity and line attractor dynamics after Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing (Mountoufaris et al. 2024)
attempts.summary: The line attractor and the shortened persistence of activity did not reproduce, and most other main findings could not be tested. The rSLDS fits explained 59% of the variance against the paper's 85%, and the paper does not describe its fitting seeds, folds or autocorrelation estimator. The behavioral effects of editing, the photometry, the slice imaging and all female-intruder results could not be tested because the dandiset does not hold them. Slightly lower male-directed activity held only when units were pooled, and the Oxtr fraction held while the Avpr1a fraction did not, with the threshold unstated. Minor checks of unaffected behavior in the imaged mice held. The file does not exist yet.
attempts.description: Tests the miniscope findings of Mountoufaris, Nair et al. (2024) on dandiset 001131, which holds z-scored VMHvl Esr1 traces and male-directed behaviour annotations of 4 control and 6 experimental male residents during interactions with a male intruder. It compares activity, behavioural selectivity, persistence (autocorrelation half-width) and rSLDS time constants between groups. The female-intruder sessions, the behaviour and photometry cohorts and the slice experiments are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.notes: Changed from blocked (other) in round 3, which agreed with the proposed change. The first run and the first revision did not find the atlas's archive, which neither the paper nor the claims file gives, and did not attempt the analysis. The second revision found it through the data links of the Kim et al. 2019 article in Europe PMC: Mendeley Data, doi:10.17632/ypx3sw2f7c.1. Its SMART-seq part gives counts per million (CPM), as Figure 1B plots, for 4,574 cells with cluster labels, of which 850 are in the eight clusters named for Esr1. Under the adopted reading (all cells of those clusters, a gene expressed at CPM above 0) 73.9% express Oxtr, inside 78 +/- 7.8%, and 49.4% of these also express Avpr1a, below 61 +/- 6.1%. Cells with Esr1 detected give the same split (73.9% and 48.6%). Male cells only (713) at CPM above 0 give 70.4% and 56.2%, both inside, near the lower edges; with a threshold of 1 CPM the male Oxtr fraction falls to 67.6%, and with 5 or 10 CPM every reading puts both values outside. Over all cells of the clusters the Avpr1a fraction is 43.6 to 49.4% under every threshold (43.0 to 48.6% for those with Esr1 detected). At CPM above 0 all eight clusters hold cells that co-express Avpr1a (the fewest, Tsix_Esr1_1, 3%), where the Results give 5 of 8, so the paper may have used a stricter criterion at least by cluster; higher thresholds lower both fractions. The paper gives no threshold and no subset of cells ("analyzed as described previously", STAR Methods, Transcriptomic analysis); that is asked of the authors (findings).
deviations: The atlas is read from Mendeley Data (doi:10.17632/ypx3sw2f7c.1), the deposit of Kim et al. 2019 found through the article's data links; neither the paper nor the claims file names it. Its SMART-seq part is used, as Figure 1B plots counts per million; the 10x part gives raw counts per sample without cluster labels.
The Esr1+ VMHvl cells are the cells of the atlas's eight clusters named for Esr1 (Esr1_1 to Esr1_6, Tsix_Esr1_1, Tsix_Esr1_2), matching the Results' "most clusters (5/8)".

Assumption. All cells of those clusters, of both sexes, with a gene expressed at CPM above 0. The paper says "~78% of Esr1+ cells in VMHvl expressed Oxtr mRNA" (Results, Most Esr1+ neurons co-express Oxytocin and Vasopressin receptors, paragraph 1), naming no sex and no threshold, and the STAR Methods (Transcriptomic analysis) refer to the atlas paper; above 0 is the most inclusive threshold and gives the highest fractions. Male cells only and thresholds of 1, 5 and 10 CPM are shown; they give different outcomes.

No measure with a defined summary differs between groups at p < 0.05 (Mann-Whitney per mouse); the smallest p over the six is 0.114 (sniff time as a percentage of the interaction). Total sniff time 89.1 s control, 93.1 s experimental (p = 0.61); sniff bout duration 10.2 and 2.5 s (p = 0.17, the control mean raised by mouse 511's two long bouts); total attack time 54.1 and 91.5 s (p = 0.25); attack bout duration 3.3 and 2.4 s (p = 0.25); latency 261 and 91 s (p = 0.25); interval between attacks 30.9 and 11.7 s (p = 0.39). Attack probability, four readings. (a) attack-triggered probability of attacking over 0 to 10 s, mean 0.45 and 0.36 (p = 0.25), the adopted reading; (b) its decay to 1/e, 4.7 and 3.0 s (p = 0.25); (c) share of the interaction attacking, 4.3 and 10.7% (p = 0.14); (d) attack bouts per minute, 0.80 and 2.79 (p = 0.036, the smallest p 3 and 5 mice allow), the experimental mice attacking more often. Under reading (d) the criterion would fail, on a difference towards more aggression, not a deficit. The claims file may misread the paper, and a reader is asked (questions/001131.yaml): in Figure S4A, panels (iii), % time attacking, and (vi), interval between attacks, carry a star, with the experimental mice more aggressive, so the paper's "no deficits" means no reduction and the criterion "none differs at p < 0.05" is stricter than the paper. Tested as the paper's reading (a variant), no measure shows a deficit on a one-sided test (smallest one-sided p = 0.086, sniff bout duration), under every reading of attack probability. The two starred measures do not differ here (p = 0.14 and 0.39) with 3 and 5 mice.
deviations: The dandiset holds 4 control and 6 experimental mice, against 5 and 7 in the paper. Mice 510 and 500 have no attack annotation, so attack measures use 3 control and 5 experimental mice.

Assumption. The attack probability of panel S4A(vii) is plotted against time (0 to 10 s) with no per-mouse summary; it is read as the attack-triggered probability of attacking over the 10 s after an attack onset, averaged over onsets, as the S3C legend lists "the number and the time-varying probability (iv-v) of attack bouts" as two measures and S2C and S3C give a decay constant ("tau attack probability"), so a bout rate is the number of bouts per time, not the probability. Its decay, the share of time attacking and the bout rate are shown as the other readings; the bout rate differs between groups.

Under the pooled reading of "nested", experimental activity in sigma is lower than control by both the Mann-Whitney and the KS test at p < 0.05 under every baseline reading and both windows (largest p 0.014 and 0.0012; baseline all, 1 min, 0.53 against 0.95 sigma, Mann-Whitney p = 0.002, KS p < 0.001, 587 control and 474 experimental units). The claims file records the paper's level as p < 0.01, which holds under the all and gap10 baselines (Mann-Whitney p 0.0002 to 0.002) but not for 1 min with the 7-s baseline (p = 0.014). On per-mouse means or medians (4 and 5 mice) no comparison reaches p < 0.05 (p from 0.06 to 0.73). Without mice 497, 510 and 500, whose clock alignment could not be established, the pooled tests still give p < 0.01 under the all and gap10 baselines, but the Mann-Whitney test with the 7-s baseline gives p = 0.051 and 0.060. The experimental mean is about half the control mean, more than "slightly". Z-scored activity is also lower when pooled (KS p = 0.009 at 1 min, 0.0005 at 2 min), but its Mann-Whitney test is not significant (p = 0.24 and 0.12).

outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds no female-intruder session, and the paper names no other archive for these data. Two of the five expected values (units tuned to sniffing females against sniffing males) need the female interaction. The male attack-against-sniff part, shown and not deciding the outcome. Under every combination run (two shuffles, pooled or per-mouse fractions, mice with or without a baseline; the two direction readings and the two traces give the same CP), attack-tuned units are fewer in experimental mice (reduction 55.5 to 82.7%), sniff-tuned units are fewer (13.8 to 83.1%) and units tuned to neither are more (2.3 to 25.4%). At most two of the three male values are inside tolerance in any combination (reassigned bouts, per-mouse means, attack 78.9% and sniff 76.8% inside, mixed 24.0% outside 18 +/- 1.8%).

With the paper's frame-wise stratified five-fold split, every control mouse decodes attack against sniffing better than every experimental mouse (C = 1, 0.994 against 0.934; C = 0.1 and 10 alike), and the Mann-Whitney test across mice finds the difference at p = 0.036, the smallest p that 3 and 5 mice allow. With 31 units drawn per mouse in each repeat the difference is larger (0.12 to 0.13) and still at p = 0.036 for every C, so unit counts do not explain it. The measure is weak. The frame-wise split leaves frames of the same bout in training and test sets, so decoders trained on shuffled bout labels score 0.981 to 0.988 (control) and 0.904 to 0.925 (experimental) over C, far above the paper's 50% chance, and real and shuffled accuracy do not differ in either group at any C or unit count (p from 0.10 to 1.0). With whole bouts held out (a variant), accuracy is 0.79 and 0.53 against shuffled 0.53 and 0.50, and the groups differ at p = 0.036. The shuffled decoders also separate the groups (p = 0.036 with 31 units at every C; 0.036, 0.071 and 0.25 with all units), so the group difference exists without behaviour labels: the outcome follows the criterion, but the measure does not show that decoding of behaviour is impaired. Without mouse 497, whose clock alignment could not be established, every comparison gives p = 0.057 or more, the smallest p 3 and 4 mice allow, while every control mouse still decodes better than every experimental mouse.
deviations: The dandiset holds 4 control and 6 experimental mice, against 5 and 7 in the paper. Mice 510 and 500 have no attack annotation; 3 control and 5 experimental mice are used.
The cross-validation scheme is the stratified five-fold split the claims file takes from the sex decoder; the SVM's C is not given, and C = 0.1, 1 and 10 all give the same outcome.
Shuffled decoders are repeated 20 times per mouse, not 1,000; they do not decide the outcome.
Units are not subsampled in the paper's method; a variant with 31 units per mouse (the smallest count among these mice) is shown and gives the same outcome.

outcomes.notes: Under all four seeds the emissions reconstruction explains 59.4% of the variance in control and 58.4 to 58.7% in experimental mice (range 49.5 to 66.4% over mice), against 85 +/- 8.5%. The forward-prediction R2 does not differ between groups (p = 0.114 at 1 s and 5 s for every seed). Attack frames fall mostly in one state in 7, 8, 8 and 8 of the 8 mice with attack annotations (seeds 0 to 3), and at least 90% in one state in 3, 2, 3 and 5. Checks for seed 0 (rslds_checks.ipynb). Sigma-normalized fits explain 69.0% (control) and 63.6% (experimental), and their forward R2 differs between groups (p = 0.016). On held-out frames the reconstruction explains 47.9% and 41.0%, and forward predictions of the activity do not differ over 1 s (p = 0.26) but do over 5 s (0.371 against 0.198, p = 0.010). So the claim's "similar performance" part also fails on the held-out score at 5 s and on the sigma-normalized fits (p = 0.016 at both horizons); it holds on the in-sample score and the held-out score at 1 s. The 85% may be a measure other than the emissions R2; that is asked of a reader (questions/001131.yaml). The fits of mice 510 and 500 do not recover the authors' latent factor 1 (|Spearman r| at most 0.47 for dimension 1, 0.70 for any dimension). Seeds 0 and 1 are in rslds_seeds_0_1.ipynb and seeds 2 and 3 in rslds_seeds_2_3.ipynb, with the same cells and tags; rslds_checks.ipynb holds the seed-0 sigma-normalized fits and a held-out score.

The experimental values are two to three and a half times the paper's 9.86 +/- 1 s in every combination. Measured gives the first combination (window-mean biased estimator, seed 0, largest weight). The z-scored and sigma readings of the trace give the same ACHW under the window-mean estimators (an affine map does not change the autocorrelation), and with one intruder per file the mean over trials is the single autocorrelation; the readings left are the two unit assignments.

The estimator of the autocorrelation is not given (the paper cites Remedios et al. 2017). The window-mean biased estimator (the standard sample autocorrelation) is used, and the n - k and file-mean estimators are shown; all give the same outcome.

Unit weights on a dimension are |C Re(v)| for the eigenvector v of the reading (a) state. When the two slowest eigenvalues are a complex pair (4 to 8 of 10 mice per seed), dimension 2 takes |C Im(v)|, the other axis of the plane in which the pair rotates; the first run gave both dimensions the same weights.
The whole interaction is taken from the first annotated behaviour to the end of the file.

outcomes.notes: Over the first 1 or 2 min the reduction is 15 to 31% under every estimator and both means (window mean removed and divided by n, 14.6 and 15.9% pooled, 19.2% per mouse; divided by n - k, 15.5 to 20.2%; no mean removed and divided by n - k, 24.8 to 31.5%), against 50.9 +/- 5.1%. Experimental units are shorter with units pooled (Mann-Whitney and KS p < 0.001 under every estimator), but not across mice (p from 0.07 to 0.26). A synthetic check shows the window-mean estimators shorten a known ACHW of 10 to 30 s to 4 to 11 s over 1 to 2 min, which compresses group differences; the no-mean estimator comes within 30% of the truth at 2 min but leaves 46 to 81 units undefined. Over the whole recording (a variant, not the claim's window) the reduction is 43 to 47%. The outcome is not robust to the estimator. The undefined units of the no-mean estimator are the slowest and more of them are control units (50 against 31 at 1 min, 34 against 12 at 2 min), so leaving them out understates the reduction. Set to the window's length, a lower bound, they give a reduction of the mean of 27.6 and 34.5% pooled (24.8 and 31.7% over mice), still outside tolerance; the median, which this censoring does not bias, falls by 49.6 and 53.3%, inside it, but the claim's measure is the mean. Without mice 497, 510 and 500, whose clock alignment could not be established, the reduction over 1 to 2 min is 5 to 18%.

"Nested" tests are not defined; both readings of the claims file are run, units pooled and per-mouse means (or medians for KS claims).
The dandiset holds 4 control and 6 experimental mice, against 5 and 7 in the paper.
The z-scored and sigma readings give the same ACHW under the window-mean estimators, and the trial reading is the single autocorrelation, so the window readings and the estimator are what differ.

The estimator of the autocorrelation is not given (the paper cites Remedios et al. 2017); three are run (window mean removed and divided by n or by n - k, and no mean removed and divided by n - k, on the z-scored trace). All give the same outcome.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds the miniscope data of 4 control and 6 experimental mice, where the paper reports 5 and 7 (STAR Methods, Micro-endoscopic data extraction). The female-intruder part of every imaging session is absent, as are the behaviour cohorts of Figures 2 and 3, the fiber photometry and the slice imaging, although the paper's data statement says the source data will be deposited at DANDI. 20 of the 36 claims cannot be tested for these reasons.

The files mark neither the 5-min pre-intruder baseline, nor the intruder's entry and removal. The paper's activity measures are in units of sigma relative to that baseline, and Figure 6E uses the post-intruder period; here the baseline had to be assumed from the first annotated behaviour, and the post-intruder claim could not be tested. Only z-scored traces are given, not dF/F.

The files of mice 510 and 500 describe their trace as "DF/F" with "GCaMP6m". The values are z-scores (every unit of mouse 510 has mean 0 and SD 1), and the paper says the imaged mice carried "an AAV vector that encodes both the gRNAs and a Cre-dependent GCaMP8s" (Results, Single cell CRISPRoscopy imaging).

The files of mice 510 and 500 hold only sniffing annotations (series named "Ch1: sniffing"), with no attack or mounting, although the paper's exemplar mice attack. Mouse 510's sniffing bouts all fall between 179 and 279 s of a 1200-s recording.
The unit counts per group differ from the STAR Methods in the other direction from the mouse counts: 587 control units in 4 mice and 554 experimental units in 6 mice, against 585 in 5 and 546 in 7.

The two files of the earlier version 0.240826.1647 (subjects ControlMouse and MutantMouse) are the same recordings as mice 510 and 500 of version 0.260601.1203, with identical traces, sniffing bouts and rSLDS weights under different subject ids.

The group of each mouse is given only by the prefix of its subject id (ctrl, mut) and, in eight files, a keyword; there is no genotype or description of the gRNA. Nine sessions carry the same start date (2023-02-01), apparently a placeholder.
The trace of mouse 500 is not z-scored over its file (unit SDs 0.65 to 1.05, means up to 0.23 away from 0), unlike the other nine, so it was z-scored over a longer recording and then cut.

The rSLDS weights deposited for mice 510 and 500 ("latent factor 1") are not recovered by fits with the settings of the claims file: over four seeds their |Spearman r| with the weights of the first fitted dimension is at most 0.47, and with those of any fitted dimension at most 0.70. The fits' time constants are hundreds of seconds and their variance explained 59%, against 85% in the paper.

Questions for the authors. (1) Where does the pre-intruder baseline lie in each file, and when did each intruder enter and leave? (2) What are the "nested" Mann-Whitney and KS tests: GraphPad nested tests across mice, or tests on pooled units? The outcomes of fig4ef and figs4e depend on this. (3) For the rSLDS, which frames were fit, with which seeds and restarts, how were the cross-validation folds and horizon of the performance score formed, which state's dynamics matrix gives the time constants, and how are complex eigenvalue pairs (two equal time constants) treated in the line attractor score? (4) How is ACHW computed (which estimator of the autocorrelation, whether the window's mean is removed, over which window)? (5) How is the attack probability of Figure S4A(vii) computed and summarized per mouse? (6) Mouse 511 has two sniffing bouts of 22 and 40 s; is that annotation complete? (7) For Figure 1E, which cells of the Kim et al. 2019 atlas were counted (both sexes, or male cells only) and above what expression threshold? The outcome of fig1e depends on both.
The Results give n=4 control mice for Figure 4E-F, while the Figure 4 and S4 legends and the STAR Methods give 5. The dandiset holds 4 control mice.

disagreements.reason: Cell 16, no listed measure reaches p < 0.05, but attack measures cover only 3 control and 5 experimental mice. "Attack probability" is undefined. Read as attack bouts per unit time, it separates the groups completely; experimental mice attack more, p = 0.036 (problem 4, it was run under only one undeclared reading, the share of time attacking).

Cell 18, no difference with the "all" and "gap10" baselines or on per-mouse means. With the 7 s baseline the pooled test gives p at most 0.0001, so the outcome depends on a reading the paper leaves open.

The notebook calls it blocked, but cell 23 already decides it. The paper's test (nested Mann-Whitney) finds male sniff and attack not lower at p < 0.05 under any reading (p 0.11 to 0.79). The claim needs all four directions, so it fails whatever the female data show (problem 1).

entries.title: VMHvl Esr1 activity and line attractor dynamics after Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing (Mountoufaris et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the miniscope findings of Mountoufaris, Nair et al. (2024) on dandiset 001131, which holds z-scored VMHvl Esr1 traces and male-directed behaviour annotations of 4 control and 6 experimental male residents during interactions with a male intruder. It compares activity, behavioural selectivity, persistence (autocorrelation half-width) and rSLDS time constants between groups. The female-intruder sessions, the behaviour and photometry cohorts and the slice experiments are not in the dandiset.
